subject: Science
title: Natural and made things
objectives: Children will sort objects into natural and made with support.
Children will name materials such as wood, cloth and plastic.
content: Things from nature, things people make, and sorting natural and made things.
teachingActivities: Use real objects such as leaves, stones, wood, cloth and plastic; say what each thing is made of; keep the sorting simple with two baskets; link to what children see around the school.
learnerActivities: Sort objects into natural and made and name materials such as wood, cloth and plastic.
resources: Leaves, stones, shells, sticks, a flower
A plastic cup, a cloth, a wooden spoon, a metal key, a toy car
Pictures of natural and made things
assessment: Observe whether each child sorts objects into natural and made with support and names two materials.
expectedOutcomes: Sorts objects into natural and made with support.

lessons.title: Things from nature
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name things that come from nature.
successCriteria: Names a leaf, a stone and a stick
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials as wet, dry, soft, hard, rough and smooth and know about plants and animals.
lessons.starter: Hold up a leaf and say "This is from nature. A tree made it. Nobody made it in a factory."
teacherActivities: Show each natural object and say its name.
Say "These come from nature: trees, rocks, shells, water."
Go outside and find natural things in the yard.
Put the natural things in a basket and name them.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children touch each object.
Child finds a leaf, stone or stick.
Child puts an object in the basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each natural object and say its name. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "These come from nature: trees, rocks, shells, water." Children: Children touch each object.
Step 3. Teacher: Go outside and find natural things in the yard. Children: Child finds a leaf, stone or stick.
Step 4. Teacher: Put the natural things in a basket and name them. Children: Child puts an object in the basket.

practical.title: Nature basket
practical.safety: Check the area for sharp objects, thorns and insects first. Use only objects larger than a child’s fist and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Point to the object together and say the name.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find five natural things.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says that natural things come from nature
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects in the basket and say "Thank you, nature."
lessons.homeConnection: Collect safe natural things on a walk with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name things that come from nature" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Things people make
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name things that people make.
successCriteria: Names a cup, a toy car and a cloth
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials as wet, dry, soft, hard, rough and smooth and know about plants and animals.
resources: A plastic cup, a toy car, a cloth, a wooden spoon and a pencil
A picture of a factory or a tailor
lessons.starter: Hold up a plastic cup and say "People made this cup. It is not from nature."
teacherActivities: Show each made object and say its name.
Say "People make these things from materials."
Look around the classroom to find made things.
Put the made things in a basket and name them.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children touch each object.
Child finds a chair or book.
Child puts an object in the basket.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each made object and say its name. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "People make these things from materials." Children: Children touch each object.
Step 3. Teacher: Look around the classroom to find made things. Children: Child finds a chair or book.
Step 4. Teacher: Put the made things in a basket and name them. Children: Child puts an object in the basket.

practical.title: Made things basket
steps: Find made things in the room.
practical.safety: Use large safe objects only and keep objects out of mouths. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Point to the object together and say the name.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what a made thing is used for.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say "People make things."
lessons.homeConnection: Look for made things at home and say who might have made them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name things that people make" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Natural or made?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will sort objects into natural and made.
successCriteria: Puts an object in the correct basket
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials as wet, dry, soft, hard, rough and smooth and know about plants and animals.
resources: Two baskets labelled natural and made
lessons.starter: Show two baskets and say "One is for natural things. One is for made things."
teacherActivities: Pick up a stone and put it in the natural basket.
Pick up a cup and put it in the made basket.
Let each child pick an object and choose a basket.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say natural.
Children watch and say made.
Child sorts the object.
Children name the objects.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick up a stone and put it in the natural basket. Children: Children watch and say natural.
Step 2. Teacher: Pick up a cup and put it in the made basket. Children: Children watch and say made.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick an object and choose a basket. Children: Child sorts the object.
Step 4. Teacher: Check each basket together. Children: Children name the objects.

practical.title: Natural and made sort
steps: Put two baskets on the mat.
Put it in the natural or made basket.
practical.safety: Use only large safe objects. Supervise turns and keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Offer two objects and say where each comes from.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find one more object for each basket.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is a stone natural or made?
Is a toy car natural or made?

expectedOutcomes: Sorts objects into natural and made
Says natural or made with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say "Natural and made."
lessons.homeConnection: Sort things at home into natural and made.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "sort objects into natural and made" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: What is it made of?
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name materials such as wood, cloth, plastic and metal.
successCriteria: Matches an object to its material
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials as wet, dry, soft, hard, rough and smooth and know about plants and animals.
resources: A wooden spoon, a cloth, a plastic cup and a metal spoon
Material cards: wood, cloth, plastic, metal
lessons.starter: Hold up a wooden spoon and say "This is made of wood. Wood comes from trees."
teacherActivities: Show each object and say its material.
Let children touch each object and describe it.
Match each object to a material card.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the materials.
Child says hard, soft or smooth.
Child places the object on the card.
Child says the material.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each object and say its material. Children: Children look and say the materials.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children touch each object and describe it. Children: Child says hard, soft or smooth.
Step 3. Teacher: Match each object to a material card. Children: Child places the object on the card.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What is it made of?" Children: Child says the material.

practical.title: Material match
steps: Put material cards on the mat.
practical.safety: Use only large smooth objects with no sharp edges. Supervise handling.

differentiation.support: Offer two cards and say the material first.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find three objects made of the same material.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What is the spoon made of?
What is the cup made of?

expectedOutcomes: Matches objects to materials with support
lessons.conclusion: Put the objects away and say "Wood, cloth, plastic, metal."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about what things are made of at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name materials such as wood, cloth, plastic and metal" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 6 materials check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child sorts natural and made things and names materials.
successCriteria: Sorts objects into natural and made
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials as wet, dry, soft, hard, rough and smooth and know about plants and animals.
lessons.starter: Sing the natural and made song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: natural, made and materials.
At each station ask "Natural or made?" and "What is it made of?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or gesture.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: natural, made and materials. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Natural or made?" and "What is it made of?" Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Materials stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use only safe objects.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: sorts natural and made; names materials; says where objects come from.

questions.question: Is a leaf natural or made?
What is the cup made of?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 6
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and put the baskets away.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about natural and made things at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child sorts natural and made things and names materials" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
